mc GEOGRAPHY revenue is by customer address in four regions plus hedging; the 10-K and 10-Q name no country except the United States, and no customer is over 10% of revenue (2023-2025) [pf_10k_20260205, pf_10q_20260723]. FY2025: US 48% ($194.2B), EMEA 29% ($117.2B), APAC 17% ($67.7B), Other Americas 6% ($23.9B), hedging -$0.1B, total $402.8B. Q2 2026: US 51% ($60.8B), EMEA 27% ($32.5B), APAC 16% ($19.3B), Other Americas 6% ($7.0B), total $119.8B; US was 48% in Q2 2025. Non-US share is therefore about 49% in Q2 2026 (derived), down from about 52% a year earlier; US revenue grew about 32% year on year in Q2 (60,846 vs 46,063), EMEA 15%, APAC 17%, Other Americas about 22% (derived from the facts). Revenue by region is the input for the engine's country-risk row; no country-level split below region is disclosed (gap).

mc LONG-LIVED ASSETS (property and equipment plus operating lease assets) US vs international only: 12/31/2024 $138.99B / $45.63B; 12/31/2025 $195.34B / $66.48B; 6/30/2026 $259.95B / $78.95B. International share 24.7% -> 25.4% -> 23.3% (derived): the AI build-out has been US-weighted in 2026 (US +33% in six months) [pf_10k_20260205, pf_10q_20260723]. Where the international assets sit (Taiwan, Europe, Asia) is not disclosed; neither 10-K, Q1 10-Q nor Q2 10-Q contains the words Taiwan or China.

mc EXPOSURE ANTITRUST SEARCH (US DOJ, D.D.C.): Google Search & other was $63.3B of $119.8B Q2 2026 revenue, 52.8% (derived; 10-Q Note 2). Liability ruling Aug 2024; final judgment Dec 2025 restricts how Google distributes its services and requires sharing certain search data with, and offering syndication to, certain competitors; Google appealed Jan 2026 and the court denied the stay motion as premature; DOJ and states cross-appealed Feb 2026; no loss estimable [pf_10q_20260723 Note 10, pf_10k_20260205 Item 1A]. Candidate bear mechanism: lost default placement and data advantage on up to 52.8% of revenue plus its TAC; the size of the effect is NOT evidenced (unsized, hypothesis): the share is exposed, the revenue loss is not.

mc EXPOSURE ANTITRUST AD TECH (US DOJ, E.D. Va.; Texas AGs): Google Network revenue was $7.3B in Q2 2026, 6.1% of revenue (derived), and fell 0.7% year on year (7,354 -> 7,303) and 2.3% in H1 [pf_10q_20260723 Note 2]. The 10-Q (filed 2026-07-23) says the court was still awaiting a final judgment, the DOJ proposed structural remedies, and the state AG trial in Texas follows the DOJ remedy decision [pf_10q_20260723]. Since then (see mc NEWS 2026-09): behavioural remedies, no AdX sale. The structural-breakup tail on 6.1% of revenue is therefore much smaller than at the 10-Q date, but this rests on a syndicated press report, not the court order [mc_reuters_adtech_20260917]. YouTube ads ($11.1B, 9.2%) is not named in the ad tech remedy in the sources read.

mc EXPOSURE EU (EC competition + DMA): EMEA is 27% of Q2 2026 revenue (29% FY2025) [pf_10q_20260723, pf_10k_20260205]. Sized charges in the filings: Android EUR 4.1B fine final July 2026, paid $5.2B in July 2026 (previously accrued); ad tech self-preferencing EUR 3.0B (Sept 2025; $3.5B charge in Q3 2025; bank guarantees in lieu of cash; appeal pending); AdSense EUR 1.5B annulled by the General Court in Sept 2024, EC appeal pending; short-term accrued legal and regulatory fines and settlements $17.4B at 6/30/2026, primarily EC fines [pf_10q_20260723 Note 10 and liquidity section]. New and not in the 10-Q: DMA non-compliance decisions of 2026-07-23, EUR 460M (Search self-preferencing: own shopping, hotel, transport, sports results ranked above rivals) and EUR 430M (Play anti-steering and fees), 60 days to comply, periodic penalty payments up to 5% of worldwide turnover as worded in the Commission text (the DMA article should be checked for the per-day basis) [mc_ec_dma_20260723]. The money is small against $120B quarterly revenue; the structural risk is the product changes (Search results layout, Play fees) on EMEA revenue, unsized (hypothesis). The 10-Q also lists DMA-driven Android interoperability access for third-party AI companies and search-data sharing with rivals [pf_10q_20260723 risk factors].

mc EXPOSURE OTHER LEGAL: Epic v. Google remedies are being complied with after Epic and Google withdrew their joint motion in July 2026; state AG Play settlement awaits final court approval (settlement funded to escrow May 2024); PriceRunner (Klarna) Stockholm Patent and Market Court damages: $2.1B accrued in Q2 2026 ($1.5B in G&A, $581M interest and costs in OI&E); Russia civil judgments with compounding penalties, not expected to be material; UK ad tech Statement of Objections (Sept 2024) open; Turkey competition investigation of ad and billing practices is a press lead only (hypothesis) [pf_10q_20260723 Note 10]. Google Play revenue is inside 'subscriptions, platforms, and devices' ($12.9B, 10.8% of Q2 revenue); the Play share is not disclosed, so the Play fee mechanism is unsized.

mc EXPOSURE SUPPLY AND POWER (AI compute): the 10-K says servers and network equipment for the technical infrastructure, 'particularly for specialized AI chips', are limited to a small number of qualified suppliers, some components come from one or limited sources, and scaling is constrained by power, water and land [pf_10k_20260205 Item 1A]. Long-term supply, energy and content commitments were $707.0B at 6/30/2026, the significant majority long-term supply agreements, to be fulfilled mostly through 2030; energy service agreements run up to 2054 with take-or-pay terms and termination fees [pf_10q_20260723 Note 10]. Capex was $44.9B in Q2 2026 and $80.6B in H1 2026 against $39.6B in H1 2025, and the 10-Q expects a significant 2026 increase [pf_10q_20260723]. Alphabet began recognising revenue from sales of TPU systems in Q2 2026 (Cloud revenue +82%, backlog $519.5B of which $513.9B Cloud) and guarantees third-party data center build-outs (the 10-Q lists financial guarantees backstopping third-party data center and power infrastructure) [pf_10q_20260723]. Candidate bear mechanism: stranded or unfilled commitments of up to $707.0B if demand or supplier delivery slips; the share that is Taiwan or any single region is NOT disclosed (no mention of Taiwan, TSMC or China in the three filings read), so a Taiwan or single-region supply disruption is an unsized hypothesis, not an evidenced exposure.

mc EXPOSURE EXPORT CONTROLS, TARIFFS, SANCTIONS: the 10-K lists tariffs, sanctions and export controls among the causes of supply shortages and system disruption but gives no sized exposure; the word China does not appear in the 10-K, Q1 10-Q or Q2 10-Q [pf_10k_20260205 Item 1A]. Law-firm summaries of January 2026 actions: BIS moved licence review for H200- and MI325X-class chips to China and Macau to case-by-case, and a 25% Section 232 tariff applies to a narrow set of advanced AI chips with exemptions including imports for US data centers [mc_mayerbrown_20260116, search excerpt only, not confirmed at the Federal Register]. Alphabet is not a named seller to China in the filings; the tariff exemption for US data-center use would cover most of its capex; non-US data center imports and the new third-party TPU system sales (customer data centers) could face licence or tariff exposure: all unsized (hypothesis). No October 2026 BIS, USTR or MOFCOM notice was found (gap).

mc EXPOSURE TAX (OECD Pillar Two): effective tax rate 19.1% for Q2 and H1 2026 (16.9% and 17.1% a year earlier), raised by deferred tax on unrealised equity gains; the January 2026 OECD side-by-side safe harbor exempts US domestic operations but not foreign subsidiaries; no material effect on the H1 2026 provision, but more countries enacting the rules could raise the effective tax rate and cash taxes; gross unrecognised tax benefits $12.1B at 6/30/2026 ($10.3B would affect the rate) [pf_10q_20260723]. Revenue is 49% non-US, so the exposed base is large; the rate impact is unsized.

mc EXPOSURE FX: about 49% of Q2 2026 revenue is outside the US; hedging gains were $106M in Q2 2026 against a $112M loss a year earlier; foreign-currency debt designated as net investment hedges was $23.8B at 6/30/2026 ($15.4B at 12/31/2025) and the company issued $31.8B of foreign-currency and $20.0B of US-dollar senior notes in 2026 up to 6/30 [pf_10q_20260723]. Cash-flow hedges carried a $614M pre-tax gain to be reclassified to revenue within 12 months.

mc NEWS 2026-07-23 European Commission fines Google EUR 890 million under the DMA (EUR 460M Search, EUR 430M Play), 60-day compliance period (about 2026-09-21), same day as the 10-Q, which still describes the DMA matter only as the March 2025 preliminary findings with no estimable loss. Whether the fines were accrued, appealed or complied with is not yet in any filing read [mc_ec_dma_20260723, pf_10q_20260723].

mc NEWS 2026-08-06/07 prospectus supplements (424B5, 424B2, FWP) and 2026-08-10 8-K Items 8.01 and 9.01: $25.0B of US-dollar senior notes closed, ten tranches from floating-rate 2028 notes ($0.75B) through 6.500% notes due 2066 ($2.5B), including 4.500% 2028 ($1.25B), 4.625% 2029 ($2.0B), 4.875% 2031 ($3.5B), 5.200% 2033 ($2.5B), 5.450% 2036 ($4.5B), 6.250% 2046 ($3.0B), 6.375% 2056 ($4.5B); the 8-K names no use of proceeds [mc_8k_20260810]. With the 2026 notes through 6/30 ($20.0B US-dollar plus $31.8B foreign-currency) the 2026 senior-note issuance is about $76.8B (derived sum), plus the June 2026 equity raise of $49.6B net (Class A and C stock and mandatory convertible preferred) and a $40.0B at-the-market program, none sold at 6/30 [pf_10q_20260723]. Feeds the capital_bridge and dilution questions; the long tranches (to 2066) show the funding is long-dated. This is the only 8-K filed after the 10-Q; the filings list through 2026-10-15 shows no later 8-K or 10-Q (Form 4 and Form 144 filings were not read).

mc NEWS 2026-09-02 ad tech remedies (E.D. Va., Judge Brinkema): per Reuters she rejected the DOJ request that Google sell the AdX exchange and ordered behavioural remedies: websites using Google's ad server need not use AdX, real-time bid access from AdX for other publishers' ad servers, a compliance monitor with narrower oversight than the government sought, in place for six years (the DOJ and states asked 15), applied globally; the 106-page opinion was unsealed 2026-09-16; Google disagrees with the liability ruling and will appeal; the DOJ is reviewing its options; proposed final judgment due within 30 days of the unsealing, status unknown [mc_reuters_adtech_20260917]. A lead from a syndicated Reuters copy: confirm the order text on the docket before it backs a driver.

mc NEWS 2026-07/10 Q2 guidance and capex: press search excerpts (not registered, no date, not independent confirmation) say Alphabet raised 2026 capex guidance to $195-205B from $180-190B and expects a significant increase again in 2027; the filings confirm H1 2026 capex of $80.6B and Q2 $44.9B [pf_10q_20260723]. gather_documents owns the guidance record; confirm the range at the call transcript.

mc NEWS 2026-10-28 Q3 2026 results: one search excerpt (Benzinga, undated, not an issuer announcement) gives Oct. 28 as the Q3 report date, i.e. the day after as_of. Results of that date are not citable for this run (not until 2026-10-30); the analyst should treat 2026-10-27 as the day before results and, if the owner wants the print included, ask for a rerun with as_of 2026-10-30 or later. Not confirmed at the issuer's IR page.

mc NEWS no other material item found 2026-07-23 to 2026-10-27 in the searches made (five searches: general Alphabet legal/trade, Q3 date and capex, ad tech remedy, EU DMA, BIS and tariffs): no new export rule, tariff action or management change was found, and the filings list shows no further 8-K Item 5.02. Absence in a bounded search is not proof of absence.
